items.title: US attacks Iran's Qeshm island in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: TEHERAN: The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran's southern Island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said. "The sounds of five to six explosions were heard on Qeshm on Tuesday evening," IRNA said. Earlier in the day Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a drone attack targeting a radar system in Bahrain operated by the United States.

items.title: US lawmakers to question Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang over China chip scandal on Dec 1
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang is to appear before three US House committees on Dec 1, lawmakers said Tuesday, after a spy scandal forced him to quit and the government to tighten export curbs on chips. "The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous (Chinese) actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal." Huang will appear before all three committees in one day.

items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang open to returning as CEO as board sets up security panel
items.summary: Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Huang's statement. Earlier in the day Nvidia created a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang left. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said.

items.title: Batu Pahat crash: Teenage girl among two burnt to death
items.summary: The victims, a 17-year-old boy and a 22-year-old girl, were believed to have been trapped inside a Proton Saga BLM when it caught fire at 7.50pm. He said the two injured victims were trapped in their vehicle before being extricated by firefighters using special equipment. Based on witness accounts, two victims were trapped and burnt to death inside the vehicle.

items.title: Selangor revenue hits RM3bil, surpasses target
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor has recorded RM3 billion in revenue to date, surpassing the state's RM2.8 billion target set in its previous state budget, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. On another matter, Amirudin said the state government plans to improve people's living standards through a new approach that goes beyond existing poverty measurements. Amirudin said the state government was therefore formulating a decent living or dignified living approach to ensure that assistance provided could genuinely help lift people out of poverty.

items.title: Floods hit 'flood mosque' in Kuala Selangor again
items.summary: Mosque committee member Hasan Md Rasol, 62, confirmed the incident when contacted. He said mosque management members immediately mobilised a clean-up and rescue effort after Isyak prayers to move items, including carpets, prayer mats and copies of the Quran, to safer locations. "As at 9.40pm, floodwaters had covered almost the entire mosque compound.

items.title: Voter-roll deletions leave some Indian Muslims facing detention, deportation
items.summary: Fakir said plainclothes officers detained her, seized her phone, which she said contained copies of identity documents, and forced her across the border. Fakir is among 10 families that Reuters interviewed whose relatives were detained, deported or questioned over their citizenship after being dropped from India's revised electoral rolls. The voter list revision struck 130 million names nationwide in the largest deletion of voters in India's history.

items.title: Trump acknowledges Anwar's role in Cambodia-Thailand peace deal
items.summary: MANILA: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's commitment and cooperation in securing the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord between Cambodia and Thailand last year. He said his cooperation with Anwar during last year's Asean Summit had resulted in a historic agreement that led to a ceasefire between the two countries. Trump said Washington remained committed to upholding the ceasefire and ensuring the full implementation of the agreement.

items.title: Brexit's old battle lines return as UK seeks EU reset
items.summary: AS United Kingdom leader Andy Burnham prepares for a crunch European Union summit this week, familiar faces from Britain's Brexit wars are back, seeking to scupper his determination to forge closer ties to the bloc. Ahead of the meeting, pro-Brexit voices from the 2016 vote are reorganising, concerned by Burnham's reset plans and flirting with the idea that Britain could one day seek to rejoin the EU. "The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain," Burnham said, reiterating his criticism that it has made the country poorer and contributed to higher immigration.

items.title: Queen arrives in Turkiye for COP31
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has arrived in Antalya, Turkiye, to attend the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31). According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page today, Her Majesty's special aircraft landed at Antalya Airport about 3pm local time (8pm Malaysian time). Her Majesty was accompanied by Tunku Temenggong of Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim and was received upon arrival by Malaysian Ambassador to Turkiye Adlan Mohd Shaffieq and Turkish Foreign Ministry representative Ambassador Deha Erpek.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia must protect athletes after retirement
items.summary: THERE are two positive outcomes for elite athletes once they retire: they take on roles in the sports system that made them great or they exploit their fame and contacts to become entrepreneurs. In contrast, several former elite athletes ploughed their winnings and government perks into sustainable entrepreneurship. Over generations, Malaysia has produced countless world-class athletes.

items.title: Sewerage sector could generate new revenue through circular economy, says Fadillah
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said this approach not only optimises high-capacity sewage management but also has the potential to generate new revenue while supporting the nation's water resource sustainability. Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation (Petra) minister, said that so far, fertiliser products derived from sewage biosolids produced by Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) Sdn Bhd have obtained halal certification and are being used in the agricultural sector, including vegetable farming. Also present were Petra deputy secretary-general (water sector) Datuk Mohd Rodzwan Mohd Baba Sakri, Petra deputy secretary-general (energy sector) Datin Mareena Mahpudz, and Bernama news service deputy editor-in-chief Mohd Shukri Ishak.

items.title: Singapore takes over Asean chairship from Philippines for 2027
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippines formally handed over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to Singapore, concluding its year-long leadership of the regional bloc. Marcos said he was confident Singapore, as Asean chair in 2027, would lead with "a clarity of purpose, steadiness and commitment to regional cooperation". "Today marks the ceremonial transition of the Asean chairship to Singapore for 2027.

items.title: Trump hails 'victory' as US, Thailand sign trade statement
items.summary: The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data. "Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports" and "remove substantial non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry," Trump said. Thailand will also buy "an estimated US$2.6 billion in additional US agricultural products", he added.

items.title: Kepong parang attack: Injured policeman held fire to protect public, Bukit Aman reveals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A police Lance Corporal held his fire during a parang attack in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, on Nov 11 to protect bystanders from stray bullets, Bukit Aman said. Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said the officer was entitled to defend himself against a life-threatening attack. Noor Hisam said the 26-year-old officer had acted in accordance with police standard operating procedures (SOPs) during the emergency.

items.title: Wanted fraud suspect found hidden under luggage in car at Malaysia-Thailand border
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A Thai man was arrested for allegedly smuggling a woman wanted in a fraud case from Malaysia into Thailand by concealing her beneath a pile of luggage in his vehicle. A Thai security spokesman said the 39-year-old was driving a Toyota Fortuner when officers from the Sadao Immigration Department stopped him at the AC2 inspection lane of the new Sadao Immigration Complex at about 4.50pm yesterday. "They then discovered the woman concealed beneath a pile of luggage, without any travel documents," the spokesman said.

items.title: Man who threatened Wisma Darul Aman guard with knife to be charged tomorrow
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: A man arrested for trespassing into Wisma Darul Aman and pulling a knife on a security guard on Sunday will be charged at the Alor Setar Magistrate's Court tomorrow. Kota Setar police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said the man would face two charges involving possession of a dangerous weapon in a public place and criminal trespass. Earlier reports said the 45-year-old suspect was arrested after entering the Wisma Darul Aman compound without stopping at the security checkpoint before pulling a knife on a guard.

items.title: Widow recalls late policeman's unusual request for hot Nescafe
items.summary: TAPAH: Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob's unusual request for hot Nescafe this morning became his wife's last memory of him before he was killed in a police van crash along the North-South Expressway (PLUS) today. His wife, Nor Ilyanie Abd Aziz, 26, said she usually prepared iced Nescafe for him whenever he was on duty or travelling long distances. "I had already made iced Nescafe, but he asked for it hot instead.

items.title: Six hurt after MMEA truck skids off road in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) personnel and two undocumented migrants escaped with minor injuries after the truck they were travelling in skidded off the road near Peringat here today. Kelantan MMEA director Maritime Captain Kamal Mohamad said the incident occurred at 11.30am in Padang Mokan. Kamal said the four MMEA personnel, comprising two men and two women, and the two detainees, both Bangladeshis, did not sustain serious injuries.

items.title: Israel set to elect Netanyahu opponent as parliament speaker
items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, has put forward his ally Matan Kahana to be the next speaker. Netanyahu's Likud party is expected to try to draw out debate to scuttle Kahana's election in the parliament, known as the Knesset. Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the 120-member Knesset in Oct 27 elections.

items.title: Esscom officer's wife claims she was stripped, assaulted during police questioning
items.summary: Vivien Fabian, 38, the 14th plaintiff's witness, testified that a female officer from Bukit Aman had ordered her to remove her clothes one by one before making her squat facing a wall for several minutes in an interrogation room at the Tawau district police headquarters. Under further questioning by lead counsel Datuk Ram Singh, Vivien alleged that another male officer covered her eyes with a face mask before slapping both her ears. Vivien was seen crying several times while testifying about the alleged abuse and matters involving her children.

items.title: Asean, China reaffirm South China Sea declaration pending code of conduct
items.summary: MANILA: Asean and China remain committed to the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea until a long-awaited code of conduct is finalised, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said on Tuesday. "Until the code of conduct is ready, until it is finalised and signed by all parties, by Asean and China have pledged to follow the declaration's guidance." Marcos said Asean and China had reaffirmed their commitment to complete negotiations on a substantive and effective code of conduct consistent with the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

items.title: Ahmad Yakob appointed new Pas Mursyidul Am
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Former Kelantan menteri besar Datuk Ahmad Yakob has been appointed the new Mursyidul Am of Pas, replacing Datuk Hashim Jasin. The Pas Syura Ulama Council also appointed Johor Pas commissioner Datuk Dr Mahfodz Mohamed as deputy Mursyidul Am, while Demit assemblyman Mohd Asri Mat Daud was named the council's new secretary. Pas central Ulama Wing chief Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party appreciated Hashim's contributions, sacrifices and commitment throughout his tenure since 2016.

items.title: Macron's visit puts Rafale back in Malaysia's MRCA fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: France's Rafale fighter jet is among the options being assessed as Malaysia explores its future combat aircraft requirements, following discussions to deepen defence cooperation between Kuala Lumpur and Paris. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the aircraft was among several proposals discussed during his bilateral meeting with French Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs Catherine Vautrin at Wisma Perwira ATM earlier today. The twin-engine, multirole fighter is designed for air superiority, air defence, ground attack, reconnaissance and anti-ship missions.

items.title: Three men nabbed in cable theft attempt in Taman Seri Sentosa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three men were arrested after police found them inside a utility manhole during an operation to investigate an attempted cable theft in Taman Seri Sentosa here yesterday. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the operation began at 4pm after police received public information about suspicious activities at the location. "A team from the Petaling police station task force, assisted by other police personnel, inspected the location and found two men inside the utility manhole.

items.title: Make health insurance mandatory for UNHCR-registered refugees, govt urged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should require all refugees registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to have health insurance, to ease the financial burden on public healthcare facilities. Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said UNHCR should take responsibility for refugees issued with its cards by ensuring they were insured when seeking treatment at government hospitals and clinics. He said the increase of 7,907 occurred despite the Cabinet's July 23 directive for UNHCR to temporarily stop registering new refugees.

items.title: Trump, Thai PM to announce trade progress, not final deal
items.summary: BANGKOK: US President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand's premier on Tuesday marking "significant progress" in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said. A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes. The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: French investment sought Malaysia is seeking greater French investment, particularly in rare earth processing, as both countries look to deepen economic ties and expand cooperation in strategic sectors. Macron visits Petaling Street Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim took Emmanuel Macron on an informal visit to Petaling Street during the French president's official visit to Malaysia. Ismail resigned voluntarily Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Umno did not instruct Ismail Lasim to resign as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar, adding that the decision was made voluntarily.

items.title: SC unveils Sukuk Prisma for climate adaption and resilience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) today introduced Sukuk Prisma to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilise capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities. In a statement, the SC said the framework expands the capital market's scope beyond conventional green and social categories to encompass broader climate adaptation, resilience and transitional financing, including flood mitigation, coastal protection, agriculture and the resilience of power grids. The SC will issue the Sukuk Prisma Framework in the first quarter of 2027.
